blogs.title: Federal Circuit Rejects Inconsistent Standards of 'Similarity' Across DuPont Factors
blogs.description: This post will analyze the court's core holding that the TTAB committed legal error by applying inconsistent definitions of 'similarity' across different DuPont factors. The Board found the parties' services 'highly similar' under factor two (similarity of goods), but then restricted its factor six analysis to only credit card services marks, excluding banking and financial services. The post will discuss how this ruling reinforces the need for doctrinal consistency in multi-factor tests and prevents litigants from 'having their cake and eating it too' by strategically narrowing or expanding definitions to favor their position.

blogs.title: Third-Party Marks and Commercial Strength: Clarifying the Scope of Factor Six After Apex Bank
blogs.description: This post will examine the Federal Circuit's clarification of the sixth DuPont factor, which considers third-party marks as evidence of a mark's commercial weakness. The court held that 'similar' goods under factor six need not be identical, and—critically—that the Board must apply the same scope of similarity it used in analyzing factor two. The post will also explore the evidentiary threshold question the Board raised: whether nine third-party marks is insufficient to show weakness, compared to the 14-26 marks found sufficient in prior cases like Jack Wolfskin and Juice Generation.

blogs.title: From Credit Cards to Online Banking: TTAB's Finding of 'Legally Identical' Services Reflects Financial Services Convergence
blogs.description: This post will discuss the Board's finding—affirmed by the Federal Circuit—that credit card services and 'banking and financing services' are 'legally identical, in part,' and the implications for trademark prosecution in the financial sector. The Board relied on dictionary definitions and third-party registrations showing that modern financial institutions commonly offer both services under a single mark. The post will consider how this ruling reflects industry reality, where traditional banks, fintech companies, and credit card issuers increasingly occupy overlapping market spaces, and what practitioners should take away when drafting identification of goods and services in this sector.
